transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Hello, this is calling from our company. Is this a good time to talk about your account?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.message: What the hell kind of question is that? You think I *ever* have time for this bullshit? Call me about my account—yeah, real original. You people don’t care about me, you just want to squeeze more out of someone who’s already got nothing!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message:
I hear you, and I appreciate you being honest about how you're feeling. I know this isn’t an easy situation, and I’m not here to add stress to your day. My name is ${agent_name}, and I work with ${company_name} to help people who are going through tough times get back on track with their accounts—without judgment.

You're right—calling about your account probably isn’t the most original conversation, and I get that it might feel like just another hassle. But my goal isn’t to pressure you or “squeeze” anything out of you. It’s actually the opposite. I want to understand what you’re dealing with right now and see if we can find a way forward that works for *you*. 

If now isn’t a good time, I can call back later—no problem. But if you’re open to it, I’d really like to listen and see how we can make this manageable. You don’t have to go through this alone.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.message:
Oh, spare me the "I feel your pain" act, alright? You don’t know the first thing about what I'm dealing with. Everybody's got sob stories, but rent don’t care, the lights don’t care, and your damn company sure as hell didn’t care when they slapped on late fees while I was begging for time!

But fine—*talk*. What the hell do you wanna know? That I got laid off two months ago? That I’m digging in the couch cushions just to eat? Go ahead, write it down. Just don’t sit there pretending you give a damn.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message:
You're absolutely right—I *don’t* know everything you're going through, and no, I haven’t walked in your shoes. I won’t pretend I have. And you're also right that the system often feels cold, unfair, and stacked against people when they’re already down. The late fees, the calls, the pressure—it all adds up, and I see how that can feel like salt in the wound.

I’m not here to judge, and I’m not here to make excuses for how things got to this point. What I *am* here for is to see where you are *now*—because what matters most to me in this moment isn’t the past, it’s whether we can find a way forward that doesn’t break you.

So yeah, if you’re willing to share, I’d like to understand:  
How are you managing right now?  
Is there any income coming in, even if it’s temporary?  
And if we were to come up with a payment plan—something realistic, something *doable*—what would that look like for you?

I can’t promise miracles, but I *can* promise to work with what you tell me. And if you’re not in a place to pay anything right now, I still want to know—because we might be able to set up a temporary pause or adjust things until your situation improves.

You don’t have to believe I care—but I *am* listening. And I’m not going anywhere until we figure out the next step, together.
